claims.role: Governor-General of Taiwan under Japanese colonial administration

geographicScope.description: Taiwan governed as a Japanese colonial administration, the assigned historical entity; governor is a colonial officeholder, not an elected president or head of an independent Taiwanese state.

evidence.note: National Central Library biography identifies the sixteenth Japanese Taiwan governor, office beginning May 1932 and ending September 1936. This continuous tenure contains the complete 1935 calendar year; month endpoints preserve the departure precision.
Permanent exhibition Japanese-rule section independently places Taiwan within Japanese conquest and colonial rule after 1895. It supports colonial scope only; it does not supply this governor’s term.

cautions: Civilian governor status does not imply a sovereign democratic state or universal representative government. The selected-year claim does not adjudicate present sovereignty.

sources.institution: National Central Library, Taiwan Memory; Chang Tzu-wen / 張子文
sources.title: 中川健藏 — Taiwan historical biographies (Ming, Qing and Japanese-rule period)
sources.usage: Full biography description and bibliography body read: Japanese sixteenth Taiwan governor; appointed May 1932, took office 27 May, left September 1936. Continuous four-year/four-month tenure supports all of selected 1935. Appointment and successor endpoints are not guessed; other-title romanization is not used as name evidence.

reviewNotes: Full 1935 interval is justified by a continuous sourced 1932–1936 tenure, not a single-date attestation or raw polygon date.
Chinese personal name is the institutional biography heading; Nakagawa Kenzō is conventional Japanese transliteration. The catalogue other-title form Nasegawa Kenzo is not adopted.

Departure is supplied only as September 1936 in the read biography; no exact September day is asserted. Detailed appointment disputes outside 1935 are not needed to establish selected-year incumbency.
Existing b02-taiwan-museum URL/ID is reused for colonial context; no falsely broadened governor-specific source usage or duplicated URL.
